page: Microsoft Azure E64-32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Eadsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory density of 16.0 GB per core.

This server includes 3780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable. It does not feature any GPU accelerators. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 vector extensions (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16), cryptography acceleration (AES, VAES, SHA_NI), and virtualization via AMD SVM.

Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in single-core stress-ng CPU tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Passmark CPU, encryption, and extended instruction tests rank in the strong tier, alongside multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and small-model LLM inference text generation. However, multi-core stress-ng CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall into the average tier. Large-model LLM text generation is a notable performance bottleneck, scoring in the bottom tier.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and fast local NVMe SSD storage, the E64-32ads_v7 is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, large databases, and data caching systems. Its qualitative cost efficiency is driven by the high resource density of memory and local NVMe storage relative to the dedicated compute allocation, making it a strong fit for enterprise database hosting, memory-bound analytics, and single-thread intensive processing tasks.
